old_summary: A client library for connecting agents to a tool service caches identity tokens at module level without keying them by intended audience. If an application uses it to authenticate to two or more services in the same process, a token minted for one sensitive service can be sent to another service. Someone who operates, compromises or monitors traffic to that second service can capture the token and replay it to impersonate the application against the first. Precondition: multiple audiences used in one process. The record lists a network attack vector, attack requirements present, no privileges and no user interaction. The attacker acts directly from the receiving service.
new_summary: A client library for connecting agents to tool services caches identity tokens without separating them by intended audience. When an application authenticates to multiple audiences in one process, a valid, unexpired token issued for one service can be reused in a request to another. An attacker who operates, compromises or monitors traffic to the receiving service can capture the token and replay it against its intended service to impersonate the application. Preconditions include multiple audiences sharing the process and a reusable token remaining valid. The application's requests trigger the cache mistake; the source describes attacker receipt and replay, without identifying attacker-supplied input that triggers the initial reuse. The record lists network access, additional attack requirements, no privileges and no user interaction.
